title: Kitchen and Orchard
premise: When pastry chef Ines Vane discovers her late grandmother's will names her co-inheritor of a failing orchard on a remote island — alongside Theo Marsh, the estranged son of the woman her family blamed for everything — she arrives intending to sell and save her café. But the deed carries a condition: neither heir can sell unless both stay through one full harvest, and the orchard's old foreman is quietly maneuvering to seize it for himself. As Ines and Theo rebuild the harvest together, they uncover letters proving their families' feud was built on a lie, forcing each to choose between the safe lives they've constructed and a future — and a love — that demands the whole heart. On the last ferry of the season, Ines must decide whether to board it or stay and claim the orchard, the café's new home, and Theo.
about_author: Oscar Delacroix is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade in island kitchens before turning to fiction. Their novels pair food writing with slow-burn romance, exploring how inheritance shapes identity.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Ines Vane's POV. Her café fails its third bank review; that night a lawyer's letter reveals she's inherited half an orchard on Ferrow Island. She plans to sell immediately. Emotional beat: desperation disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Other Name
chapters.summary: Ines reads the deed and finds a second name: Theo Marsh, son of the woman her family blamed for her grandmother's ruin. She calls the lawyer demanding answers. Emotional beat: old grudges rekindled by paperwork.

chapters.title: Theo Marsh, Arriving Late
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He learns of his mother's death and the inheritance he never wanted, arriving on the island hungover and grieving. He meets Ines at the orchard gate; they recognize each other's surnames instantly. Emotional beat: grief colliding with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Condition
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. The lawyer explains the will: no sale until both heirs complete one full harvest together. Theo wants out; Ines needs money fast. Neither can leave without the other. Emotional beat: trapped allies.

chapters.title: Foreman Bram
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Orchard foreman Bram Kessler offers to 'manage things' for them, hinting he'll buy them out cheaply. Something in his smoothness unsettles her. Emotional beat: first whiff of corruption beneath kindness.

chapters.title: First Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Reluctantly staying, Theo works the trees and discovers he loves the physical labor — and notices Bram's crew cutting corners, bruising fruit. He says nothing yet. Emotional beat: unexpected belonging.

chapters.title: Flour on the Ferry Dock
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines bakes from the orchard's apples at a dockside stall to raise cash; it sells out. Theo helps unasked, and their first real conversation happens over a shared crate. Emotional beat: grudging warmth.

chapters.title: Bram's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds discrepancies in Bram's accounts — sales recorded as losses. When he questions Bram, he's smoothly warned off. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Locked Room
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finds her grandmother's locked study and, inside, a half-burned letter mentioning Theo's mother by name — not with blame but with love. She hides it, shaken. Emotional beat: foundations cracking.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A storm flattens a section of orchard; working through the night side by side, Ines and Theo cross a line from allies into something tenderer. A near-kiss interrupted by Bram. Emotional beat: intimacy under pressure.

chapters.title: What Her Family Said
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts Ines about what her family did to his mother — driving her off the land, per his father's dying words. Ines defends her grandmother; they fight bitterly. Emotional beat: trust wounded.

chapters.title: The Café Deadline
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The bank gives Ines thirty days. Bram offers her a private buyout of her share only — enough to save the café if she abandons the harvest and Theo. She doesn't answer him. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a helpful face.

chapters.title: Letters in the Wall
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Repairing storm damage, they open a cavity in the farmhouse wall: decades of correspondence between their grandmothers, revealing they were partners — in the orchard and in love — until Bram's father forged documents to turn them against each other. Emotional beat: the lie exposed.

chapters.title: Bram Moves
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Realizing the heirs know too much, Bram files a claim challenging the will's validity and cuts the crew's wages to force collapse. The harvest stalls. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed.

chapters.title: Rallying the Island
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines turns her dockside stall into a community kitchen; islanders who loved the grandmothers volunteer for the harvest. Theo organizes crews. Emotional beat: a found family forming.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Both POVs. On a night off, Ines and Theo finally give in to each other — then Ines, terrified of losing control, pulls away and admits she was considering Bram's buyout. Theo walks out. Emotional beat: self-sabotage at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the county hearing on Bram's claim, the forged documents are produced — and Ines testifies about the letters, choosing truth over her own escape route. The claim collapses. Emotional beat: courage over safety.

chapters.title: Bram Unmasked
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. With the claim dead, the islanders' testimony exposes Bram's ledger fraud to the whole community; he's dismissed and leaves vowing the orchard will fail anyway. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The bank deadline arrives the same day as the final ferry. Ines boards it with her suitcase — then, at the rail, chooses to disembark, betting everything on converting the farmhouse into the café's new home. Emotional beat: the whole heart, risked.

chapters.title: Harvest Day
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The full community brings in the last of the crop; Ines serves apple pastries from a folding table where the café will stand. Theo asks her, plainly, to build something with him. Emotional beat: joy earned.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Deed
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They amend the deed so both names remain — not as prisoners of the will but as partners. Ines writes to her family telling the true story of the grandmothers. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Kitchen and Orchard
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. Spring: the café opens its doors facing the blossoming rows. Ines measures her life no longer in safe steps but in seasons shared. Final beat: inheritance transformed — what was a burden becomes a home.
